beats.text: Hi — I'm walking you through ROR World. It's the marketplace built for Ruby on Rails talent and the companies hiring them.
This is the public job board. Curated Rails roles from teams around the world — search, filter, and apply without noise from other stacks.
Employers show up in the company directory, so candidates can see who's hiring and dig into each brand.
Now the candidate side. Developers sign in to a personal hub — applications, saved jobs, and profile progress in one place.
They search for Rails roles, open a job, apply in one click, and save anything they want to revisit.
Every candidate also gets Track Applications — a lightweight personal ATS across Applied, Screening, Interview, and Offer. Useful when you're interviewing at more than one company.
Switching to hiring. Recruiters land on a dashboard with posted jobs, applicants, and open talent at a glance.
They keep a recruiter profile current, add their company brand, then publish a Rails role — title, skills, salary, and location. From blank form to a live opening in a couple of minutes.

My Jobs keeps openings organized. On the Applications board, recruiters review candidates on a Kanban pipeline. Open any card for the resume and profile, update status, and leave a note for the hiring team — all without leaving the workflow.
And when you need more pipeline, browse the talent marketplace, save strong Rails profiles, and build a shortlist. That's ROR World — connecting Rails talent with the teams that need them.
